methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $35M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Remedy Robotics, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by David Bell and Jake Sganga, has raised $35M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public company (277810.KQ), including peers such as Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics across Seed through Series B stages.

Two methods triangulate the valuation. The stage-progression approach applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $35M raised proxy, implying $70M. The peer-median method references three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B, Walden Robotics at $1.1B), yielding a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.1B to $1.8B. This wide divergence reflects the methodological gap between early-stage capital-based approaches and late-stage peer multiples.

The triangulated analysis produces a range of $60M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $860M. The disparity between stage-progression ($70M) and peer-median ($1.6B) reflects tension between capital-based valuation and comparable company multiples at different maturity stages. Key uncertainties include whether peer valuations at Series B and Seed stages appropriately anchor a Series A position, and whether the peer set's manufacturing focus and capital intensity align with Remedy's specific technology and go-to-market trajectory.
